plan.chapterName: OpenStax Organic Chemistry, chapter 28: Biomolecules: Nucleic Acids
plan.contextChunk: This figure diagrams RNA transcription as a flat schematic of three nucleic acid strands drawn as tapered colored ribbons. A blue-violet ribbon runs across the top, labeled "DNA sense strand", marked 5' at its left tip and 3' at its right; a cyan ribbon runs along the bottom, labeled "DNA antisense strand", marked 3' at left and 5' at right. Both ribbons bow away from each other through the middle of the figure to open a bubble, and outside the bubble at each end their bases pair through vertical dot columns, C with G, A with T, and T with A at the left, G with C, A with T, and C with G at the right. Inside the bubble the sense strand's bases hang free and read T C A G C T G G C T G A A C G C G T T, while the antisense strand's exposed bases are hydrogen bonded to a magenta ribbon lying between the two, labeled "mRNA" by a leader line at its right end and marked 5' at left and 3' at right; its magenta bases read U C A G C U G G C U G A A C G C G U U. Placing the new transcript directly against its template makes the base-by-base complementarity readable in one glance, and comparing it upward with the blue-violet strand shows the two agree except that U stands wherever the sense strand carries T.

elements: Blue-violet tapered ribbon (DNA sense strand) running left-to-right across the top, with arrow-notched tips at both ends
Cyan tapered ribbon (DNA antisense strand) running left-to-right across the bottom, with arrow-notched tips at both ends
S-shaped bends in both DNA ribbons that bow them apart to open the central transcription bubble
Magenta/pink tapered ribbon (mRNA transcript) lying in the middle of the bubble, blunt arrow tips
Short vertical tick stubs projecting from each ribbon representing bases (blue-violet on sense, cyan on antisense, magenta on mRNA)
Left flanking duplex region: three vertical dot-columns (hydrogen bonds) pairing sense C-A-T with antisense G-T-A
Right flanking duplex region: three vertical dot-columns pairing sense G-A-C with antisense C-T-G
Sense-strand letters inside the bubble: T C A G C T G G C T G A A C G C G T T (19 bases, hanging free, no pairing dots)
Antisense-strand letters inside the bubble: A G T C G A C C G A C T T G C G C A A (19 bases)
mRNA letters inside the bubble: U C A G C U G G C U G A A C G C G U U (19 magenta bases)
Vertical dot-columns (hydrogen bonds) between each mRNA base and the antisense base directly beneath it
5' label at left tip and 3' label at right tip of the sense strand (black)
3' label at left tip and 5' label at right tip of the antisense strand (black)
5' label at left tip and 3' label at right tip of the mRNA (magenta)
Text label 'DNA sense strand' upper-left with leader arrow pointing to the sense ribbon bend
Text label 'DNA antisense strand' lower-left with leader arrow pointing to the antisense ribbon bend
Text label 'mRNA' lower-right with leader line pointing to the right end of the magenta ribbon

interactions.teaches: The antisense strand is the template: as the open bubble advances along the duplex, each newly exposed template base dictates one complementary ribonucleotide, and the mRNA elongates strictly 5'→3'.
interactions.label: Transcription position (bases synthesized)

interactions.teaches: Which two strands are being compared changes what complementarity means: DNA–DNA uses A–T, DNA–RNA uses A–U, and the sense strand is identical to the transcript except T is replaced by U.
interactions.label: Base-pairing view

interactions.teaches: Each individual base has one partner and one strand polarity; hovering shows which strand is read and which base the transcript carries at that position.

demo_steps.title: Closed duplex
demo_steps.narration: Before transcription the sense (blue-violet) and antisense (cyan) strands are paired end to end; note the antiparallel 5'→3' labels and the dot columns marking hydrogen bonds.

demo_steps.title: Bubble opens, RNA begins
demo_steps.narration: The strands bow apart and RNA polymerase reads the antisense strand 3'→5', laying down the first ribonucleotides: template A gives U, G gives C, T gives A.

demo_steps.title: Transcript elongates
demo_steps.narration: The bubble advances; behind it the DNA would reclose, while ahead new template bases are exposed. The magenta strand grows only at its 3' end.

demo_steps.title: Full transcript
demo_steps.narration: All 19 template bases have been read. The mRNA reads 5'-UCAGCUGGCUGAACGCGUU-3'.

demo_steps.title: Sense strand vs mRNA
demo_steps.narration: Compare upward: the mRNA matches the sense strand base for base, except every T is replaced by U — which is why the sense strand is also called the coding strand.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Flat 2D schematic in the XY plane, viewed front-on; no depth. World span x ∈ [-14, 14], y ∈ [-4, 4] (aspect ≈ 3.4:1, matching the very wide source). Base columns spaced 1.0 unit apart. Left flanking duplex columns at x = -12, -11, -10 (sense letters C, A, T above; antisense G, T, A below; three small vertical dots between them at y ≈ 0 spanning y = -0.45..0.45). Bubble base columns: 19 columns at x = -8.5, -7.5, ... , +9.5. Right flanking duplex columns at x = +11, +12, +13 (sense G, A, C; antisense C, T, G). Sense ribbon: thickness 0.38, centered at y = +2.55 across the bubble (x from -9.2 to +10.2), stepping down through an S-bend to y = +1.35 at the flanks (x < -9.4 and x > +10.4), ending in arrow-notched tips at x = -13.9 and +13.9. Antisense ribbon is the mirror image about y = 0: y = -2.55 in the bubble, y = -1.35 at the flanks. mRNA ribbon: thickness 0.34, straight, centered at y = +0.75, spanning x = -9.3 to +10.0 only (never enters the flanking duplexes). Base tick stubs are 0.45-long rectangles of width 0.10 pointing inward from each ribbon toward the strand it faces. Letter rows: sense bubble letters at y = +2.0 (just below the top ribbon's ticks); mRNA letters at y = +0.2 (below mRNA ribbon, magenta); antisense bubble letters at y = -0.55; hydrogen-bond dot columns (3 dots) between mRNA letters and antisense letters at y ≈ -0.15..-0.40; antisense ticks rise from the ribbon at y = -2.55 up to y ≈ -1.0. Sequences, left to right: sense bubble T C A G C T G G C T G A A C G C G T T; mRNA U C A G C U G G C U G A A C G C G U U; antisense bubble A G T C G A C C G A C T T G C G C A A. Colors: sense ribbon blue-violet #6a7fc0 at ends fading to pale #cfd8f0 at center (horizontal gradient, lightest mid-bubble); antisense ribbon cyan #23bdee at ends fading to pale #bfeafb at center; mRNA ribbon #ec2f8c at left/right ends fading to #fbd0e4 at center; ribbon ticks match their ribbon's saturated color; all DNA letters and dots black #000; all mRNA letters and its 5'/3' labels magenta #ec2f8c; annotation text black ~0.5 units tall with thin black leader arrows: 'DNA sense strand' at (-12.5, 3.6) arrow to (-9.6, 2.0); 'DNA antisense strand' at (-11.5, -3.6) arrow to (-9.0, -2.3); 'mRNA' at (11.5, -2.4) leader up-left to (9.6, 0.5). Background white.
interactionPlan.notes: Render entirely with orthographic camera facing -Z (flat 2D); build ribbons as extruded THREE.Shape paths (rounded rect body + S-bend via quadratic curves) with vertex-colored or canvas-texture horizontal gradients to reproduce the pale-center shading. Base letters and 5'/3' labels as sprite/canvas text or troika-text so they stay crisp at this wide aspect; keep a single text atlas per color. Hydrogen-bond dots are small circle instances. For the transcription slider, clip the mRNA ribbon's right end and hide mRNA letters/ticks beyond index n, and animate the DNA bubble opening by interpolating the S-bend control points so unopened regions to the right stay paired (show their DNA-DNA dot columns) — implement bubble edges as two movable bend positions. Hover: invisible picking planes (~0.9 × 1.2 units) over each base column; on hover, dim all other columns to 25% opacity and draw a highlight box plus a small callout giving base identity, strand name, and 5'/3' direction. pairingView toggle only changes which dot columns / letter highlights are emphasized — geometry is unchanged: 'DNA–DNA' highlights the flanking dot columns, 'DNA–RNA' highlights the bubble mRNA↔antisense dots, 'Sense vs mRNA' draws faint vertical connector lines between sense and mRNA letters and outlines the T→U positions in magenta.

authoredContext:
Following formation of the polymerase–promoter complex, several turns of the DNA double helix untwist, forming a bubble and exposing 14 or so base pairs of the two strands. Appropriate ribonucleotides then line up by hydrogen-bonding to their complementary bases on DNA, bond formation occurs in the 5′ → 3′ direction, the RNA polymerase moves along the DNA chain, and the growing RNA molecule unwinds from DNA (the figure). At any one time, about 12 base pairs of the growing RNA remain hydrogen-bonded to the DNA template.

Biosynthesis of RNA using a DNA segment as a template.

Several turns of deoxyribonucleic acid double helix unwind exposing bases of the two strands. Ribonucleotides line up such that hydrogen bonds form in 5-prime to 3-prime direction.

Unlike what happens in DNA replication, where both strands are copied, only one of the two DNA strands is transcribed into mRNA. The DNA strand that contains the gene is often called the sense strand, or coding strand, and the DNA strand that gets transcribed to give RNA is called the antisense strand, or noncoding strand. Because the sense strand and the antisense strand in DNA are complementary, and because the DNA antisense strand and the newly formed RNA strand are also complementary, the RNA molecule produced during transcription is a copy of the DNA sense strand. That is, the complement of the complement is the same as the original. The only difference is that the RNA molecule has a U everywhere that the DNA sense strand has a T.

discrepancies: In the default 'DNA–RNA pairs' view the black hydrogen-bond dot columns of the closed flanking duplex are dimmed to ~25% opacity, so the prominent solid dot columns (C:G, A:T, T:A) that read clearly in the source appear faint/washed out at first glance.
The mRNA base letters render with reduced opacity (vis*eMr fading) and so appear paler pink than the saturated magenta letters in the source; end letters of the bubble fade most.

The 'mRNA' caption and its leader arrow are placed tight against the right-hand antisense flank letters (C/T/G), producing slight crowding that the source avoids by placing the caption well below and to the right.
Sense-strand tick stubs above the bubble are somewhat shorter relative to the letter spacing than in the source, where the ticks are long and visually dominant along the top ribbon.
evaluation.notes: A very close reproduction of the transcription diagram with correct sequences, antiparallel 5′/3′ labeling, ribbon shapes and colors, plus a rich and pedagogically sound set of interactions (position slider, three pairing views, guided demo, hover inspection); main weaknesses are the default view dimming the duplex hydrogen-bond dots and slightly washed-out mRNA letters, plus minor crowding of the mRNA caption.
action_items: Keep the flanking DNA–DNA hydrogen-bond dot columns at full opacity in all views (only de-emphasize dots inside the bubble) so the default screenshot matches the source's solid dot columns.
Render the mRNA base letters at full magenta opacity once synthesized rather than scaling opacity by the bubble profile, so they read as crisply as in the source.
Move the 'mRNA' caption further down-right and shorten/reangle its leader so it does not crowd the right flank antisense letters.
Lengthen the sense-strand tick stubs slightly to match the source's proportion of tick length to base spacing.

feedback.rationale: The concept and interaction structure are correct (concept 5, no failure modes); remaining issues are purely rendering details like opacity of dot columns and mRNA letters, caption placement, and tick length.

demo_steps.title: Closed duplex
demo_steps.narration: Before transcription the sense (blue-violet) and antisense (cyan) strands are paired end to end; note the antiparallel 5'→3' labels and the dot columns marking hydrogen bonds.

demo_steps.title: Bubble opens, RNA begins
demo_steps.narration: The strands bow apart and RNA polymerase reads the antisense strand 3'→5', laying down the first ribonucleotides: template A gives U, G gives C, T gives A.

demo_steps.title: Transcript elongates
demo_steps.narration: The bubble advances; behind it the DNA would reclose, while ahead new template bases are exposed. The magenta strand grows only at its 3' end.

demo_steps.title: Full transcript
demo_steps.narration: All 19 template bases have been read. The mRNA reads 5'-UCAGCUGGCUGAACGCGUU-3'.

demo_steps.title: Sense strand vs mRNA
demo_steps.narration: Compare upward: the mRNA matches the sense strand base for base, except every T is replaced by U — which is why the sense strand is also called the coding strand.

Antisense ribbon is the mirror image about y = 0: y = -2.55 in the bubble, y = -1.35 at the flanks. mRNA ribbon: thickness 0.34, straight, centered at y = +0.75, spanning x = -9.3 to +10.0 only (never enters the flanking duplexes). Base tick stubs are 0.45-long rectangles of width 0.10 pointing inward from each ribbon toward the strand it faces. Letter rows: sense bubble letters at y = +2.0 (just below the top ribbon's ticks); mRNA letters at y = +0.2 (below mRNA ribbon, magenta); antisense bubble letters at y = -0.55; hydrogen-bond dot columns (3 dots) between mRNA letters and antisense letters at y ≈ -0.15..-0.40; antisense ticks rise from the ribbon at y = -2.55 up to y ≈ -1.0. Sequences, left to right: sense bubble T C A G C T G G C T G A A C G C G T T; mRNA U C A G C U G G C U G A A C G C G U U; antisense bubble A G T C G A C C G A C T T G C G C A A. Colors: sense ribbon blue-violet #6a7fc0 at ends fading to pale #cfd8f0 at center (horizontal gradient, lightest mid-bubble); antisense ribbon cyan #23bdee at ends fading to pale #bfeafb at center; mRNA ribbon #ec2f8c at left/right ends fading to #fbd0e4 at center; ribbon ticks match their ribbon's saturated color; all DNA letters and dots black #000; all mRNA letters and its 5'/3' labels magenta #ec2f8c; annotation text black ~0.5 units tall with thin black leader arrows: 'DNA sense strand' at (-12.5, 3.6) arrow to (-9.6, 2.0); 'DNA antisense strand' at (-11.5, -3.6) arrow to (-9.0, -2.3); 'mRNA' at (11.5, -2.4) leader up-left to (9.6, 0.5). interactionPlan.notes: Render entirely with orthographic camera facing -Z (flat 2D); build ribbons as extruded THREE.Shape paths (rounded rect body + S-bend via quadratic curves) with vertex-colored or canvas-texture horizontal gradients to reproduce the pale-center shading. Base letters and 5'/3' labels as sprite/canvas text or troika-text so they stay crisp at this wide aspect; keep a single text atlas per color. Hydrogen-bond dots are small circle instances. For the transcription slider, clip the mRNA ribbon's right end and hide mRNA letters/ticks beyond index n, and animate the DNA bubble opening by interpolating the S-bend control points so unopened regions to the right stay paired (show their DNA-DNA dot columns) — implement bubble edges as two movable bend positions. Hover: invisible picking planes (~0.9 × 1.2 units) over each base column; on hover, dim all other columns to 25% opacity and draw a highlight box plus a small callout giving base identity, strand name, and 5'/3' direction. pairingView toggle only changes which dot columns / letter highlights are emphasized — geometry is unchanged: 'DNA–DNA' highlights the flanking dot columns, 'DNA–RNA' highlights the bubble mRNA↔antisense dots, 'Sense vs mRNA' draws faint vertical connector lines between sense and mRNA letters and outlines the T→U positions in magenta.

plan.authoredPrompt: This figure diagrams RNA transcription as a flat schematic of three nucleic acid strands drawn as tapered colored ribbons. A blue-violet ribbon runs across the top, labeled "DNA sense strand", marked 5' at its left tip and 3' at its right; a cyan ribbon runs along the bottom, labeled "DNA antisense strand", marked 3' at left and 5' at right. Both ribbons bow away from each other through the middle of the figure to open a bubble, and outside the bubble at each end their bases pair through vertical dot columns, C with G, A with T, and T with A at the left, G with C, A with T, and C with G at the right. Inside the bubble the sense strand's bases hang free and read T C A G C T G G C T G A A C G C G T T, while the antisense strand's exposed bases are hydrogen bonded to a magenta ribbon lying between the two, labeled "mRNA" by a leader line at its right end and marked 5' at left and 3' at right; its magenta bases read U C A G C U G G C U G A A C G C G U U. Placing the new transcript directly against its template makes the base-by-base complementarity readable in one glance, and comparing it upward with the blue-violet strand shows the two agree except that U stands wherever the sense strand carries T.

- Hover for individual bases: hover over any exposed DNA or mRNA base, and its paired partner and strand direction labels appear, showing which strand is read and which sequence matches the transcript.

discrepancies: Vertical proportions are compressed relative to the source: the mRNA ribbon/letters, the antisense letters and the hydrogen-bond dot columns are crammed into a narrow band, whereas the source leaves clear vertical separation between the transcript row and the template row.

The transcription-bubble amplitude is shallower than in the source — the sense and antisense ribbons bow apart much less, so the open-bubble geometry reads as a thin slot rather than the tall opened duplex of the original.

In the flanking (closed-duplex) regions the paired letters (C·G, A·T, T·A on the left; G·C, A·T, C·G on the right) and their three-dot hydrogen-bond columns are squeezed together and much tighter than in the source, reducing readability of the base-pair notation.
The mRNA 3′ label and the mRNA leader arrow sit right on top of the right-hand flank letters (G/C column), colliding visually; in the source the 3′ label is clearly clear of the DNA letters.

The mRNA ribbon in the source spans the full bubble with clear blunt ends and a strong magenta→pale gradient; the generated ribbon is thinner and its gradient/tick stubs are subtler than the original's prominent pink strand.
evaluation.notes: A faithful and well-labelled recreation of the sense/antisense/mRNA transcription diagram with genuinely useful interactions (elongation slider, three pairing views, guided demo, hover base identification); main weakness is vertical compression — the bubble amplitude and the spacing between transcript, template letters and hydrogen-bond dots are much tighter than the source, and the mRNA 3′ label collides with the right flank letters.

feedback.rationale: The concept, elements, and interactions are correct; the remaining issues are implementation-level layout fixes (vertical spacing, bubble amplitude, letter spacing, and the colliding 3′ label).

5' label at left tip and 3' label at right tip of the mRNA (magenta)

discrepancies: Vertical spacing inside the bubble is compressed relative to the source: the antisense letter row sits almost on top of its tick marks and the dot columns, making that band noticeably more crowded than the airy original.

The mRNA ribbon reads as uniformly saturated magenta across most of its length, whereas the source has a strong pale-pink centre with saturated ends; the DNA ribbon gradients are closer but also slightly flatter.
Base letters and 5′/3′ end markers are rendered at a smaller relative size than in the source, where the letters are one of the dominant graphic elements of the figure.

mRNA base-tick stubs are very short stubs pointing down only; in the source the pink ticks are longer and clearly hang from the ribbon toward each letter, giving the transcript the same visual weight as the DNA strands.
evaluation.notes: A faithful, well-sequenced reproduction of the transcription diagram with correct sense/antisense/mRNA sequences, correct antiparallel end labels and leader-arrow captions, backed by a genuinely useful slider, three pairing views, hover identification and a five-step guided demo; weaknesses are cosmetic — crowded vertical spacing in the bubble, undersized base letters, and flatter ribbon gradients than the original.
action_items: Increase the vertical gaps between the antisense ribbon, its ticks, the dot column and its letter row so the bubble band matches the open spacing of the source.
Raise base-letter and 5′/3′ label font size (and keep caption labels visibly larger/bolder) to restore the source's typographic hierarchy.
Strengthen the pale-centre gradient on the mRNA (and DNA) ribbons so the middle of each strand washes out as in the original.
Lengthen the magenta mRNA tick stubs so each nucleotide letter is visibly attached to the transcript ribbon, matching the DNA tick treatment.
